story.title: Trump Administration Proposes New Tariffs on Multiple Trading Partners
story.summary: The Trump Administration has proposed new tariffs targeting 14 major trading partners, including China and the European Union. This move is seen as a response to perceived unfair trade practices and could escalate existing global trade tensions. Countries affected by the proposed tariffs have been informed of the plans.

explore_lenses.label: Why does this matter for U.S. trade policy?
explore_lenses.title: A broad new use of Section 301
explore_lenses.summary: The proposal shifts the administration’s tariff strategy toward country-specific Section 301 cases after earlier broad tariffs were invalidated. It would cover major suppliers and U.S. allies, not China alone.

claims.text: USTR found the manufacturing-capacity practices of 14 economies—including China, the EU, Japan, South Korea, India, Taiwan and Vietnam—actionable under Section 301; it made no determination yet for Mexico or Norway.
The proposed country rates range from 15% for the EU to as much as 35% for Vietnam; China would face up to 20%, subject to product-specific treatment and exemptions.

The new proposals follow the Supreme Court’s February 20, 2026 ruling invalidating certain tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act, after which the administration turned to other tariff authorities.

The European Commission rejects the premise that Europe creates structural overcapacity, while saying the EU and U.S. share concerns about state-driven overcapacity concentrated in third countries; it expects the 15% ceiling in the August 2025 EU-U.S. joint statement to be honored.

explore_lenses.label: How did the administration build this case?
explore_lenses.title: An eight-month excess-capacity investigation
explore_lenses.summary: USTR frames the cases as a response to government policies that create persistent manufacturing output beyond market-oriented levels and disadvantage U.S. producers. The finding is an administrative determination that affected governments dispute.

claims.text: USTR opened investigations on March 11, 2026 into 16 economies’ policies on structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing; it says it received nearly 140 witness testimonies and 1,070 comments.

USTR defines structural excess capacity as capacity or production persistently above what would exist under market-oriented conditions and created, sustained or contributed to by government intervention.
Ambassador Jamieson Greer argues that industrial targeting, labor-cost suppression, financial support and non-market inputs have distorted competition and eroded the U.S. manufacturing base.
China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun called the overcapacity allegation a false issue and opposed its use as a justification for political pressure.

explore_lenses.label: What happens before any tariffs take effect?
explore_lenses.title: Comments, hearings and possible negotiation
explore_lenses.summary: The proposals now enter a formal comment process, giving importers, workers, foreign governments and other stakeholders a chance to argue for different rates or exemptions. USTR has also left room for negotiated outcomes for several partners.

claims.text: Written comments and requests to testify are due January 5, 2027, and USTR plans public hearings beginning January 25, 2027.

For several economies, USTR explicitly says the proposed rate could be adjusted in light of existing duties, ongoing consultations or a responsive reciprocal-trade agreement; examples include India, Singapore and Vietnam.
Forecast: Greer said he did not expect the proposed measures to take effect for at least a couple of months, after the comment and hearing process.

Brazil is not among the 14 economies in this excess-capacity proposal; USTR separately proposed modifications to its existing Brazil Section 301 action, including measures affecting sugar and aircraft exports.

story_report.summary: The Trump administration has proposed country-specific tariffs on 14 economies after U.S. trade officials found their manufacturing-capacity practices actionable under Section 301. The proposals would affect partners including China, the European Union, Japan, South Korea, India, Taiwan and Vietnam, with rates ranging from 15% for the EU to as much as 35% for Vietnam; China could face up to 20%, subject to product-specific treatment and exemptions. The measures are proposals rather than final actions, opening a public-comment and hearing process before implementation decisions are made.

sections.heading: Section 301 Excess-Capacity Investigations
sections.body: USTR opened investigations on March 11 into the policies of 16 economies concerning structural excess capacity and production in manufacturing. The agency says it collected nearly 140 witness testimonies and 1,070 comments. Its definition covers capacity or production that persistently exceeds market-oriented levels and is created, sustained or contributed to by government intervention. The administration turned to other tariff authorities after the Supreme Court invalidated certain tariffs imposed under the International Emergency Economic Powers Act in February.

sections.heading: Trading Partners Challenge U.S. Rationale
sections.body: U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer argues that industrial targeting, labor-cost suppression, financial support and non-market inputs have distorted competition and weakened the U.S. manufacturing base. China’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun called the overcapacity allegation a false issue and opposed using it to justify political pressure. The European Commission rejected the premise that Europe creates structural overcapacity, while saying it shares U.S. concerns about state-driven overcapacity in third countries and expects the 15% EU-U.S. ceiling agreed in August 2025 to be honored.

sections.heading: Public Process Determines Final Tariffs
sections.body: Written comments and requests to testify are due January 5, 2027, and USTR plans to begin public hearings on January 25. Greer said he did not expect the measures to take effect for at least a couple of months after that process. USTR has said rates for several economies, including India, Singapore and Vietnam, could be adjusted to account for existing duties, consultations or responsive reciprocal-trade agreements. Brazil is not among the 14 economies in the excess-capacity proposal, though USTR separately proposed changes to its existing Brazil action involving sugar and aircraft exports.

unresolved.text: Final tariff rates, covered-product exclusions and the interaction with existing duties have not been determined, because USTR has issued proposed remedies rather than final implementation notices.

It remains unresolved whether trading partners will make new commitments, whether final measures will depart from the proposals, and whether USTR’s country-specific evidence and remedy design would withstand a legal challenge.

related_stories.title: Russian Strikes Kill Seven in Ukraine; Kyiv Targets Refineries
related_stories.summary: Russian drone attacks resulted in the deaths of seven people across six Ukrainian regions, targeting infrastructure including a gas production facility and a thermal power plant. In response, Ukraine launched drone strikes on Russian oil refineries in the Samara and Rostov regions, as well as an airbase in Nizhny Novgorod, leading to at least one reported death in the Samara region.

related_stories.title: China Launches Shenzhou 24 with Two Chinese and One Pakistani Astronaut
related_stories.summary: China has successfully launched the Shenzhou 24 spacecraft, carrying two Chinese astronauts and one Pakistani astronaut. This mission marks the first time a foreign astronaut has joined a crew on a Chinese space station. The crew is set to conduct over 90 scientific experiments and technology tests during their time in space.
